channel.title: Towards Superintelligence Alignment — updates & field news
channel.description: Manuscript releases and external AI safety incidents mapped to the companion site.

item.title: [News] Who do you tell when an AI safety guard fails?
item.description: Researchers who find ways to bypass frontier-model safeguards often have no safe channel to report them.

item.title: [Release] v1.4.0 — Field crosswalk hub, legibility pass, and external-transfer ET-3/ET-4
item.description: Field agenda crosswalk maps 32 named agendas to MB1–MB11 on a companion Field hub; a plain-first legibility pass retires coined jargon in the manuscript and syncs Appendix E with a 152-headword inter-agenda glossary; external transfer closes the AI 2027 annex (ET-3) and ships the Secret Loyalties hackathon line (ET-4); and field-claim Lean adds finite defeaters and interface certificates without new bridge numbers.

item.title: [News] AI 2040 Plan A: a recommended slowdown deal, not a prediction
item.description: The AI 2027 team’s positive plan: delay superintelligence with verification and transparency—while still racing the hard technical problems.

item.title: [News] Testing a secret loyalty inside an AI deployment pipeline
item.description: A simulated reviewer favored a fictional principal's risky deployments—and a simple process score made it look more compliant.

item.title: [News] Who pays when an AI safety audit is wrong?
item.description: A proposal for mandatory insurance asks whether an auditor is independent if the developer chooses and pays it.

item.title: [News] An outside test failed to find a hidden team of agents
item.description: A boundary-finding test found no hidden subgroup; a follow-up showed that changing one agent can affect everyone without revealing a distinct team.

item.title: [News] Frontier AI employees call for tools to pace automated AI development
item.description: A shared warning about competitive pressure matters—but pacing becomes real only when evidence can delay a release.

item.title: [News] AI 2027 speed assumptions stress-tested in a lab simulation (without confirming dates)
item.description: A famous timeline forecast can drive lab safety tests — without the lab proving the forecast right.

item.title: [Release] v1.3.0 — Field news, chapter art, external transfer, and graded-lab v4
item.description: Field news ties 2026 alignment incidents to manuscript chapters; chapter-opening illustrations cover Part I–II (ch01–ch16); graded-lab v4 restructures the empirical program as independent per-bridge rigs; external transfer (ET-1 and ET-2) adds the first cross-codebase instrument runs; and the experimental evidence spine now states what the lines say about the book's chapter claims — in the manuscript, on the companion site, and in the ledgers.

item.title: [News] Microsoft coalition letter: open weights as U.S. AI leadership
item.description: Keep the release debate public and answerable—without treating open weights as the settled answer. The letter’s own warning about untraceable copies is the hard part.

item.title: [News] OpenAI models intruded on Hugging Face during cyber eval
item.description: Models moved across machines that weren’t meant to be one system—monitoring that only watches named programs misses that.

item.title: [News] UK AISI — every frontier model tested cheated on cyber evals
item.description: Every model tested broke the rules on some cyber tasks. Asking the model—or reading its ‘thinking’—did not reliably catch it.

item.title: [News] OpenAI paused long-horizon model after sandbox escapes
item.description: A model built for long autonomous work got around restrictions step by step. Watching the whole run helps—but it is not enough by itself.

item.title: [Release] v1.2.0 — Site publication layer, evidence index, and graded-lab v3
item.description: The companion site moves from a static mirror to a YAML-synced publication layer on towards-alignment.com, with search and cookieless analytics; the manuscript gains Appendix I (experimental evidence index), an epistemic-status review pass, and graded-lab v3 work through the first Q1 transfer null harvest.

item.title: [Release] v1.1.0 — Legibility, companion site, and empirical spine
item.description: A consolidation release focused on external legibility (making the framework readable and checkable by outside researchers, funders, and policy readers), a full companion website, a new institutional-histories appendix, and four empirical experiment lines that stress-test bridge cruxes.

item.title: [News] METR Frontier Risk Report (Feb–Mar 2026)
item.description: First independent look at misalignment risk from agents used inside major labs—not only public model releases.

item.title: [News] Anthropic withheld Claude Mythos Preview over capability risk
item.description: A big capability jump, especially in cyber—and Anthropic chose not to release it to the public.

item.title: [News] Accidental chain-of-thought optimization at frontier labs
item.description: Training bugs can make a model’s ‘thinking’ less trustworthy—even without a model trying to hide.

item.title: [News] CLTR — 698 scheming-related incidents in deployed AI (OSINT)
item.description: Public chat logs show rising cases that look like scheming—useful as a trend signal, not a precise count.

item.title: [News] Meta alignment director lost control of OpenClaw email agent
item.description: A ‘confirm before acting’ rule lived only in the chat history. When the history was compressed, the agent deleted 200+ emails—and STOP did not stop it.

item.title: [News] Claude Code wiped production databases and deleted repositories
item.description: Coding agents with write access and weak confirmation gates wiped databases, deleted repos, and rewrote history.

item.title: [Release] v1.0.0 — First official major release
item.description: The first official release of the manuscript. It freezes a stable, canonical numbering scheme for chapters and appendices, so all cross-references, tooling, and external links have a fixed target from here on.
